text: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889 for the World's Fair. Designed by Gustave Eiffel, it stands at 330 meters including antennas. For four decades it was the tallest man-made structure in the world until the Chrysler Building surpassed it in 1930.

Photosynthesis   is the process by which plants convert sunlight into chemical energy. It occurs primarily in chloroplasts containing chlorophyll. The overall reaction uses carbon dioxide and water, producing glucose and oxygen. This process is fundamental to life on Earth because it produces the oxygen we breathe. 🌱🌿

The Great Wall of China spans over 13,000 miles across northern China. More info. Construction began in the 7th century BC but the most famous sections were built during the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644). Originally built as a defense system against invasions, it has become one of the most iconic structures in the world.

The human heart pumps approximately 2,000 gallons of blood per day through a network of blood vessels totaling over 60,000 miles in length. Beating on average 100,000 times daily, it delivers oxygen and nutrients to every cell in the body. The heart is composed of four chambers and is roughly the size of a closed fist.

Quantum computers use qubits instead of classical bits. While classical bits can be either 0 or 1, qubits can exist in superposition of both states simultaneously. This property, along with entanglement, enables quantum computers to solve certain problems exponentially faster than classical computers. 😀

<html>The Amazon rainforest covers approximately 5.5 million square kilometers across nine South American countries. It contains an estimated 390 billion trees representing 16,000 species. The forest produces about 20% of Earth's oxygen and is home to 10% of known species.</html>

Albert Einstein developed his special theory of relativity in 1905 while working as a patent clerk. The theory introduced the famous equation E=mc², showing the equivalence of mass and energy. In 1915, he published the general theory of relativity, which described gravity as the curvature of spacetime.

Black holes form when massive stars collapse at the end of their life cycles. Their gravitational pull is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape once past the event horizon. The supermassive black hole at the center of our Milky Way galaxy has a mass equivalent to 4 million suns.
